cohort: 47 pregnant women who underwent renal transplantation and cesarean section between 2007 and 2017
finding: The study suggests that regional anesthesia (spinal) may be preferable to general anesthesia for cesarean section in pregnant women with renal transplantation, as it appears to have some advantages in terms of maintaining postoperative renal function and higher Apgar scores in newborns with low birth weight.
mod_finding: This study investigated anesthesia management in cesarean sections for pregnant women who underwent renal transplantation but did not specifically compare different modes of delivery.
